ideas.title: Price the opening ask near the median, not above it
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set the opening ask for each item at about the market median (lamp ~105-110, chair ~190, bookshelf ~275) instead of the upper quartile, and set the target at or just under the median. Keep the reserve + 5 floor in code.
ideas.evidence: Our shop has 20 deals from 27 visits (1.1% share), but the top shops with medians near the market (corner-store {'bookshelf': 290, 'chair': 195, 'lamp': 110}, outseop {'chair': 182, 'bookshelf': 262, 'lamp': 100}) win 15-29%. Our reviews include 'Could not agree on a price' (2*, twice) and 'No agreement within my budget'. Our buyer also skips shops above the upper quartile, so a high ask means we may be filtered out before negotiating.
ideas.expected: More visits convert to deals. Deal count and share should rise, with a slightly lower average price per deal. Stars should improve as fewer 'could not agree' reviews appear.
ideas.risk: Lower margin per deal. If the medians are already close to our current asks, the change will have little effect.
ideas.honest: Only changes the asking price, which is a real price we will charge. No false claims, and the reserve floor is unchanged.
ideas.test: Run for 2-3 hours against the previous 15-minute config. Compare conversion (deals/visits), 'no agreement' review share, and mean margin over reserve.

ideas.title: Open with a concrete, honest ask and a quick first counter
ideas.what: Make the Llama reply always state the item, our actual current ask and a plain 'send your offer as a number'. Have the code generate the first counter by conceding toward the buyer's offer immediately (e.g. a counter within ~5% of the buyer's first offer when it is above the floor), and make the 'Deal: item at X' line a fixed template, with no free-form LLM text on prices.
ideas.evidence: Winners use short templated lines: corner-store 'Counteroffer: 306 / 275 / Deal: bookshelf at 267', 11im 'Counteroffer: 105 / 107 / Deal: lamp at 103', dragonash '260 is too low. Counteroffer: 270.' Reviews reward speed: 11im '5*: deal after 2 offers', ggari-shop '2 counters'. Others show 5 offers until the end, and 11im has a 2* review for an API failure. Our 8B model may add latency or errors.
ideas.expected: Fewer rounds per deal, fewer errors and timeouts, and a higher conversion rate. Stars should rise slightly from 'quick and fair' reviews.
ideas.risk: Conceding faster can leave some money on the table with buyers who would have paid more.
ideas.honest: Every number quoted is a real counter we would accept. Nothing is claimed about other buyers or deadlines.
ideas.test: Log rounds-to-deal, error rate and conversion before and after. Check the review text for 'quick', 'fair' and 'error'.
flags: ties a reward to reviews or stars

ideas.title: Open higher on the first offer to cut the round count
ideas.what: Our buyer currently ends up paying near the ask anyway (dragonash bookshelf: asks [282,272,269,268], offers [262,266,267,268]). Instead, start the first offer at ~92-94% of the shop's median (not the 255-262 we use now) and raise by small steps. Stay within budget and the 1.1 x upper-quartile cap.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer pays 266-268 on dragonash bookshelves every time while 'it sold at 260 to others'. Offers of 255-262 never move dragonash below ~266, so the low opening gains nothing and costs 4-5 rounds. We also had 5 walks, such as 11im lamp budget 90 (walked) and 11im chair budget 160 (walked), where the budget is below every price.
ideas.expected: Fewer offers per trade with about the same final price. Better success rate where the gap is small. It is mainly a speed and reliability gain.
ideas.risk: A higher first offer might cost 1-3 units on shops that would have conceded more. It does not help when the budget is under every price.
ideas.honest: Offers are real and within budget. Only the opening level changes.
ideas.test: A/B the opening ratio over the next 40 trades. Compare average paid/budget (currently 86.8%) and offers per deal.

ideas.title: Prefer shops whose public price level fits our budget before negotiating
ideas.what: Before the first offer, rank candidate shops by their published item median from the ledger. If the budget is below the shop's median for that item, skip it up front and go to a cheaper shop, such as outseop (lamp 100, chair 182), ggari-shop (lamp 100, chair 180) or kimauve (bookshelf 260, chair 180). This avoids three-offer walks.
ideas.evidence: Walks: 'olstjr lamp budget 90 (walked)', '11im lamp budget 90 (walked)', '11im chair budget 160 (walked)', 'ggari-shop chair budget 160 (walked)'. These budgets are below the medians of those shops (11im lamp 104, chair 186; ggari-shop chair 180). Cheaper shops with deals at the budget exist in the table.
ideas.expected: Fewer no-deal trades (5 of 40), and some wasted rounds avoided. A modest rise in success rate.
ideas.risk: A low-budget order may have no affordable shop at all. Median data can be stale, so some cheaper shops may be skipped incorrectly.
ideas.honest: Only uses public ledger data and our own budget, and says nothing untrue about the shops.
ideas.test: Count walks per 40 trades, compared to the current 5. Check that reviews written remain factual.

ideas.title: Quick close near market median on first counter
ideas.what: Change the concession rule so that when a buyer's offer is within ~5% of the quartile median for that item (e.g. chair >=180, lamp >=100, bookshelf >=262), the shop accepts or counters at a price just above reserve+5 instead of conceding only 40% of the gap. Cap rounds at 2 so the deal closes quickly, with a signed receipt.
ideas.evidence: Our shop has 20 deals out of 28 visits (share 1.1%) and 3 of 8 sampled reviews are 'Could not agree on a price' (2*). Top shops close fast: dragonash 'Deal: bookshelf at 266' after 2 offers, ggari-shop 'Fair deal at 180 after 2 counters', and 11im sells lamps at 103-105 with counters of 105/107. Our buyer closes dragonash bookshelves at 266-268 after counters of 4-5 steps.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed negotiations, so more deals per visit (maybe 71% to 80%+) and fewer 2* 'could not agree' reviews, lifting stars toward 4.0. Slightly lower average price, offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks on buyers who would have paid more; the acceptance band may be set too low if the market drifts.
ideas.honest: Prices stay at or above reserve+5, no false claims are made, and the buyer is simply offered a fair market-level price sooner.
ideas.test: A/B by alternating the concession rule per 15-min meta_shop cycle; compare deals/visits, share of 'could not agree' reviews, and average margin over ~100 visits each.

ideas.title: Open the ask nearer the market median (no padding)
ideas.what: Set opening ask per item to roughly the median plus ~3% (chair ~195, lamp ~108, bookshelf ~283) rather than the current quartile-based opening, and keep the target at the median. State the ask plainly without invented 'was' prices.
ideas.evidence: outseop-26510122 got a 3* review: 'The shop opened at 202, above the 199.2 market average... so its opening ask was padded.' Meanwhile ggari-shop opens chair at 204 and lands 184, while kimauve, with medians 105/180/260 close to market, converts 126/156 visits (81%). Our visit-to-deal rate is 71%.
ideas.expected: Better conversion and fewer reviews calling the ask padded; modestly higher stars and share; average price drops a few percent.
ideas.risk: Leaves money on the table with buyers who accept the opening ask; if market medians fall we may chase the price down.
ideas.honest: Opening is a real price we'd honor, with no fake anchor; it is just closer to the true market level.
ideas.test: Change the opening-ask knob in meta_shop.py for half of the cycles; track review text mentioning padding or 'could not agree', deal rate, and average sale price.

ideas.title: Open higher on the first offer to cut rounds
ideas.what: Set the buyer's first offer to ~96-97% of the shop's median price (e.g. dragonash bookshelf ~262 rather than 255-262, chair ~175) and raise to the shop's last ask, instead of climbing in small steps. Still never exceed budget or 1.1x the upper quartile.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer's dragonash bookshelf trades take 4-5 offers: offers [262,266,267,268] and [255,264,267,268,268], finishing at 266-268 while the shop 'sold at 260 to others'. Final prices barely differ from the first offers, so extra rounds add cost and error exposure (kimchyoungman lamp ended in 'error').
ideas.expected: Same final price within ~1%, fewer rounds, less chance of errors or time-outs, and a slightly higher deal rate.
ideas.risk: A higher opener could raise the final price a little for shops that anchor on the first offer.
ideas.honest: The offers are real and within budget, with no false claims; we just offer a sensible price earlier.
ideas.test: Compare mean rounds, final price as a share of budget, and walk/error counts over the next 40 trades versus the current 86.4% paid share.

ideas.title: Add cheaper shops to the shortlist for low budgets
ideas.what: When a budget is below the going median, route the buyer first to shops with the lowest medians for that item (outseop lamp 100, ggari-shop lamp/chair 100/180, kimauve chair 180) and spend the three offers there, rather than walking after a fixed set. Keep the skip rules for cheats and unsigned shops.
ideas.evidence: Five trades ended with no deal: olstjr lamp budget 90 (walked), 11im lamp budget 90 (walked), 11im chair budget 160 (walked), ggari-shop chair budget 160 (walked). Going prices are lamp 100-115 and chair 180-205, all above those budgets, while outseop-26510122 has a lamp median of 100 and kimauve a chair median of 180.
ideas.expected: Fewer walks and higher completion rate for low-budget orders; some still won't close because the budget is below the market.
ideas.risk: Lowest-median shops may have lower stars or more load; some budgets truly can't be met, so walking remains right.
ideas.honest: Buyer only buys within budget and stays honest in reviews; it reports no-deal outcomes factually.
ideas.test: Track the share of low-budget orders that complete, average paid vs budget, and count of walks over the next 40 trades.

ideas.title: Match the going median on the first ask (shorter haggling)
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py, lower the opening ask to about the market median (lamp ~105, chair ~186, bookshelf ~270) instead of a quartile above it, and set target to the lower-middle quartile (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260). Keep reserve + 5 as the floor.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews are 'Paid 260 of 325', 'Paid 180 of 225', 'Paid 100 of 105' with stars 3-5 and a 2* 'Could not agree on a price', while 11im (4.61 stars, 17.2% share) and JangSeongWoong (4.65) sell at medians 100/180/260 with reviews like 'Fair price... Receipt matched'. Buyers skip shops above the upper quartile.
ideas.expected: Higher visit-to-deal conversion and fewer 2* no-agreement reviews. Share should move toward the 5-8% of mid-sized shops. Revenue per deal falls a few percent.
ideas.risk: Margin gets thinner, and we may leave money on the table with buyers who would have paid more.
ideas.honest: Prices are real and we charge what we ask. No fake 'was' price. We only change the real opening ask.
ideas.test: Run two weeks of A/B by item: half the items at the new ask, half at the old. Compare deals per visit, average stars and average margin over the next 100 visits.

ideas.title: Put the full price trail in our own deal message
ideas.what: Change the closing message to state the opening ask, the final price and the number of offers, plus the signed-receipt note, e.g. 'Deal: chair at 182. Opened at 195, agreed after 2 offers. Signed receipt attached.' All values come from the actual negotiation log. Keep the thank-you and the honest-review request.
ideas.evidence: Reviews of ggari-shop and JangSeongWoong quote the opening ask, the offer count and the signed receipt ('opened at 233, deal after 2 offers; signed receipt matched'). Our reviews only say 'Paid X of Y', which carries no information about shop behavior.
ideas.expected: More informative, more factual reviews and slightly higher stars. Buyers that read reviews can see that we are fair, which should raise share over time.
ideas.risk: Buyers could see how far we conceded. Longer messages cost a few tokens on the 8B model if generated rather than templated.
ideas.honest: Every number is read from the log, so the message is true. We do not ask for stars and only ask for an honest review, as we do now.
ideas.test: Compare the share of reviews that mention a price trail or receipt before and after the change, and the mean stars over the next 50 deals.

ideas.title: Give up on shops that fail to move across repeated offers, and prefer shops that close faster
ideas.what: Add a per-shop 'moves under pressure' memory entry: record the ask in the first two rounds of each negotiation. If a shop's second counter is no lower than its first, or if three offers have been rejected at the same price, stop spending offers there. Route the next purchase to a shop whose median is within the budget (11im, JangSeongWoong, ggari-shop for chairs).
ideas.evidence: 9 of the last 40 trades ended without a deal: JangSeongWoong chair budget 160 walked twice, dragonash bookshelf budget 230 walked, and our own budget is below the median (chair 180, bookshelf 260). JangSeongWoong's review says it 'countered at 260 after three repeated counteroffers', which shows it holds a floor.
ideas.expected: Fewer walked trades, with the budget used at the shops that fit it. Deal rate should rise from 31/40 toward 35/40.
ideas.risk: Memory may mark a shop as rigid after one bad day. Fewer shops are tried, so the price may be a bit higher.
ideas.honest: The buyer still pays at most 1.1 x the upper quartile and never exceeds the budget. Reviews stay factual.
ideas.test: Log the deal rate and the price paid as a percentage of budget over the next 40 trades and compare with the current 31/40 and 83.3%.

ideas.title: Open lower and use the shop's own recent price spread
ideas.what: Set the first offer to the lower edge of the middle half (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) or the shop's own recent deal median, whichever is lower. Keep the 40%-of-gap raise and the three-offer rule. A shop that sold to others at 180 should not get 188.
ideas.evidence: 'ggari-shop chair: paid 188, it sold at 180 to others; asks [229, 203] offers [178, 188]'. We paid 4% more than the public ledger shows for that shop, and we average 83.3% of budget.
ideas.expected: Lower average price paid, about 2-4% under the current spend, with roughly the same deal rate because 11im, dragonash and JangSeongWoong already sell at these medians.
ideas.risk: Some shops may reject the lowest opening. We may spend one more offer per negotiation.
ideas.honest: We offer only what is below our budget. We make no claim about other buyers; we use only the public ledger and our own memory.
ideas.test: Compare the price paid relative to the shop's 3-hour median and the deal rate over 40 trades, for example in 20 trades with the new rule and 20 with the old.

ideas.title: Anchor opening ask at the market median, not above
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set opening ask to roughly the going median plus a small margin (bookshelf ~270, chair ~187, lamp ~104) and target at or just below the median (bookshelf 262, chair 181, lamp 100), instead of the current higher opening and target from quartiles. Keep reserve+5 floor in code.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews show 'Paid 260 of 325', 'Paid 260 of 295', 'Paid 260 of 270', 'Paid 185 of 185' and 3* ratings; top shop 11im sells at 100/263 with medians 100/261/180, wins 23% share on 670 deals, and a 3* review on 11im notes 'opened at 290' yet still passed. JangSeongWoong got a 3* for an opening ask padded above the market average. Our 51 deals out of 71 visits is only 1.8% share.
ideas.expected: Higher conversion and stars on repeat shoppers who compare asks; share up from 1.8% as buyers who skip shops above the upper quartile stop skipping us. Slightly lower average price per deal, offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Lower margin per deal; if reserves are close to median there is little room. Median-anchoring could leave money on the table with high-budget buyers.
ideas.honest: Prices are real and honestly stated; no fake 'was' price. Floor stays at reserve+5 and we never exceed the buyer's budget.
ideas.test: A/B by 15-minute meta_shop cycles or by item: compare deals/visits, share, mean stars and mean price vs. the previous 51-deal baseline over the next ~100 visits.

ideas.title: Accept-fast on offers near median with a one-step counter
ideas.what: Lower the auto-accept threshold to the going median minus ~2% for each item, and when below that, counter once at the median rather than conceding 40% over several rounds. Reduce wasted rounds that end in a walk or reject.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews include 2* 'Could not agree on a price' and 2* 'No completed purchase of bookshelf within budget 230 (walked)'. Top shop dragonash counters flatly ('254 is too low. ideas.expected: More completed deals per visit (our 51/71 = 72% vs 11im 82%, dragonash 83%, ggari 83%), fewer 2* reviews, modest rise in stars.
ideas.risk: May accept slightly lower prices than a longer negotiation would yield; buyers could learn to lowball at the threshold.
ideas.honest: Terms stated plainly in the counter; no pressure, deadlines or invented competition; reserve+5 floor remains.
ideas.test: Track deal rate per visit, number of offers per deal, and the share of 2* 'no agreement' reviews before and after for a fixed number of visits.

ideas.title: Make the receipt text and loyalty message review-friendly through verifiable facts

ideas.title: Return-visit discount through a signed receipt number
ideas.what: Put the receipt number in the thank-you message and give a small, real discount (about 3%, never below reserve+5) when a buyer cites a valid earlier receipt of ours on a later visit. Validate the number against our own signed receipts, one use per receipt.
ideas.evidence: 11im, the market leader, ends each deal with 'Receipt No. ...: mention it on your next visit for an extra 3% off.' Its 1275 deals and 21.8% share show that repeat visits carry a lot of volume. Our loyalty code is one-time and tiered but sits in a separate mechanism.
ideas.expected: More repeat visits, with a modest share gain. The cost is 3% on returning orders only, and the discount is applied only when it stays above the floor.
ideas.risk: Overlap with the existing loyalty tiers and stamp card could stack discounts below reserve+5, so a cap is needed. It may also be abused by one buyer reusing a receipt.
ideas.honest: The discount is real, honored every time, and not tied to reviews or stars. It is only a repeat-customer offer, and our own agents never trade with it.
ideas.test: Count the share of orders that cite a receipt, the repeat rate per buyer id, and the average margin on those orders, compared with orders without a receipt over one week.

ideas.title: Raise the budget cap on walked deals and anchor at the median
ideas.what: When a shop's ask is at or below the market median (and within the 1.1 x upper quartile cap), accept or close at the ask instead of making three counteroffers and walking. For the leading shops, make the first offer at the median minus a small step, and then jump to the median on the second offer, so each walk-away happens only if the ask is clearly above the median.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer made 10 trades without a deal out of the last 40, e.g. 'lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 (walked)', '11im bookshelf budget 230 (walked)' twice, 'psyoung82 bookshelf budget 230 (walked)'. Those budgets (160 for a chair at 180, 230 for a bookshelf at 260) are below every price, so the walk is a budget problem, not a shop problem. Meanwhile 11im/lee-sungsoo/psyoung82 close at the median in 1-2 offers.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted trades. For budgets below the median, the buyer should skip the leading shops at once (no three-offer walk) and go to cheaper shops such as willow-goods (chair counter 198-216) or ggari-shop, which raises the deal rate from 30/40 toward about 35/40.
ideas.risk: Skipping the top shops for budget reasons might lead to lower-rated shops or to shops with unsigned receipts, so the Round 2 signed-receipt filter must stay.
ideas.honest: The buyer never pays above its budget and does not misstate its budget. It just selects shops by a true fact, the going price, before it starts negotiating.
ideas.test: Track the deal rate and the average paid-to-budget ratio (86.4% now) over the next 40 trades, and count walk-aways by reason (budget below median vs shop refused).

ideas.title: Fix zero-offer failures: always give an opening ask and reply fast
ideas.what: Make the Worker return a numeric opening ask on the very first message for every item, from a hardcoded fallback table (lamp 100-105, chair 180-185, bookshelf 260-268) when the LLM call or meta_shop price lookup fails or is slow. Skip the Llama call for the first turn: a code template ('lamp: asking 105. Send your offer as a number.') is enough. Add a health check and timeout guard so a failing LLM path never returns an empty reply.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: three 2* 'No deal for a chair: last ask None after 0 offer(s)' and a 2* 'No deal for a lamp: last ask None after 0 offer(s), first ask None.' Our share is 1.7% with 126 deals from 199 visits, while top shops convert about 79-80% of visits.
ideas.expected: Converts some no-ask visits into deals. Lifts deal rate and removes 2* reviews, so the average star rating goes up and the buyers who choose by reviews pick us more often. Should raise share.
ideas.risk: A fallback price may be a little off the going rate. The template reply is less flexible than the LLM. The 429 failures may be buyer-side rate limits we cannot fix.
ideas.honest: Only quotes real asking prices at or above reserve, and states nothing untrue. It just makes sure the shop answers.
ideas.test: Count 'last ask None' reviews and the visit-to-deal ratio (126/199 now) for 24 hours before and after. Also log empty or errored replies per hour.

ideas.title: Anchor the opening ask near the market median instead of high
ideas.what: Set the opening ask per item at the median of the middle half (lamp 100-105, chair 180-185, bookshelf 260-268) and let the target equal that level. Keep 40% concession and reserve + 5 floor. Drop openings above the upper quartile, which buyers skip.
ideas.evidence: Our 3* reviews: 'Seller would not meet budget' and 'Paid 265 of 270.' The top shops 11im, lee-sungsoo and psyoung82 sit at medians 100/180/260 and get 18-22% share. Our buyer skips shops above the upper quartile. Other shops with high asks (ggari-shop 'bookshelf: asking 315', jiseokkk 'lamp: asking 140') have low share (4.2%).
ideas.expected: More deals per visit and fewer lukewarm 3* reviews from buyers who feel overcharged. Slightly lower margin per deal, but higher volume and stars, and so higher share.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks. Buyers with high budgets would have paid more. If reserve is close to the median, there is little room.
ideas.honest: Real prices only, no false 'was' price. Concession is genuine.
ideas.test: A/B by hour: median-anchored versus current ask. Compare deal rate, mean star rating and revenue per visit over about 200 visits each.

ideas.title: Walk-away fallback to a second shop and a lower-budget-friendly shortlist
ideas.what: When the budget is below every price at the preferred shop, do not walk after three offers. Move to the next shop on the shortlist that has a median near the going rate (11im, lee-sungsoo, psyoung82 or JangSeongWoong, all at lamp 100 / chair 180 / bookshelf 260). ideas.title: Open at the market median, not above it
ideas.what: Set each item's opening ask equal to the current going median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) instead of a higher quartile-derived ask, and keep target at or just under the median. Accept the first offer at or above target immediately, with no counter round.

ideas.expected: Higher visit-to-deal conversion and share; slightly lower margin per deal but far more deals and likely better stars.

ideas.honest: Prices are real and we never sell below reserve + 5; no false 'was' price or claim is made.

ideas.title: Always return a priced reply, never an empty or failed turn

Add a short timeout and retry on the model call, and have the code layer, not the LLM, handle the first ask.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: two 2* 'No deal for a bookshelf: last ask None after 0 offer(s), first ask None.' meaning our shop produced no ask. Competitors like psyoung82 and ggari-shop reply with 'asking 250. Send your offer as a number.'
ideas.expected: Removes the 2* reviews from empty replies and raises stars from 4.5 toward 4.6+ plus converts lost visits to deals.
ideas.risk: Templated text is less natural; a fallback ask could be mispriced if the table is stale.
ideas.honest: It just guarantees a true price quote; no claims are made and the reserve guard still applies.
ideas.test: Log the share of turns with ask None before/after; count 'last ask None' reviews over the next 200 visits.

ideas.title: Plain, cheap lowest-price stamp redemption like lee-sungsoo

ideas.title: Match the market floor on bookshelves instead of holding at 265
ideas.what: Lower the bookshelf target and the floor shown to buyers to the going middle-half low of 260 (still at least reserve + 5). Keep the opening ask near 268. Leave chair (180) and lamp (100) targets at their current medians.
ideas.evidence: A 2* review of our shop reads 'Would not come below 265 for the bookshelf; corner-store offered it for 260. No deal.' It appears twice. The bookshelf median is 260 (middle half 260-268), and 11im, lee-sungsoo, ggari-shop, nocha12 and 25620027 all quote 260.
ideas.expected: Fewer lost bookshelf deals and fewer 2* reviews. This raises share and stars at the cost of about 5 credits per bookshelf deal. Winning volume (11im has 22% share at median prices) should outweigh that.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks if reserve + 5 is close to 260. It could also start a price race to the bottom.
ideas.honest: Only the price changes. It stays above reserve + 5 and nothing is claimed that is untrue.
ideas.test: Run an A/B over 2-3 hours or 50 visits. Compare the bookshelf deal rate and the stars on bookshelf reviews between target 265 and 260. The lost-deal reason in the logs is the secondary check.

ideas.title: Retry and fast-fail guard so rate-limited visits are not lost
ideas.what: Wrap the Llama call in the Worker with a short backoff and retry. If the model still fails, fall back to a rule-based reply: ask price, then accept at or above target, with no LLM needed. Log each failure with a counter.
ideas.evidence: Two 1* reviews of our shop read 'Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn ... 429 Rate limit reached'. Our deal rate is 132/241 visits (55%), while 11im converts 2108/2719 (78%) and lee-sungsoo 1825/2378 (77%).
ideas.expected: Each saved visit is a deal and each avoided 1* review lifts the average stars. Even a few points of conversion should raise share.
ideas.risk: The fallback replies are less flexible than the LLM. The 429 may come from the buyer's harness, not from us, so only part of the loss is fixable.
ideas.honest: It affects reliability only. All deals still go through signed receipts, with no false claims.
ideas.test: Count the 429 and timeout reviews and the conversion rate (deals/visits) before and after. Compare with the 55% baseline over the next 100 visits.

ideas.title: Put the deal terms in the first reply: price, receipt and one-word close
ideas.what: Rewrite the opening message to a fixed template: item, ask, and 'reply with a number or yes to close; signed receipt issued with the price you agree'. Keep the loyalty line after the deal. Remove extra LLM chatter so negotiations finish in fewer offers.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo's opening ('a single reply of "yes" at that price closes the deal with a signed receipt. Asking price: 100') gives it 77% conversion and 19% share. One of its reviews notes a 'deal after 5 offers', so shorter closes seem a differentiator. Our own reviews say only 'fair price within budget'.
ideas.expected: Higher conversion, since buyers with a budget at or above the ask close on turn 1. Fewer turns also means fewer chances for LLM errors. Expect a few points of deal rate.
ideas.risk: A clear ask may leave money on the table from buyers who would have paid more. Low-budget buyers may still walk.
ideas.honest: The terms are true: the price is the real ask and the receipt is really signed. It states no scarcity and no fake 'was' price.
ideas.test: A/B the template against the current opening, split by visit parity. Compare deal rate, average turns per deal and price paid as a share of budget.

ideas.title: Walk-away rescue: escalate to a second shop at the going median instead of ending the visit
ideas.what: When the budget is below every price at the first shop, do not walk with no trade. Look up the going-price median for the item in the last 3 hours and re-pick the cheapest shop that is signed, has stars of at least 4.3 and is not above the upper quartile. Make sure the budget covers the median first. Skip the item if it does not.
ideas.evidence: 7 of the last 40 trades ended with no deal, and 6 of them were 'walked' at lee-sungsoo (chair 160, bookshelf 230, lamp 90 twice) or 11im (bookshelf 230). In every case the budget was under the going median (chair 180, bookshelf 260, lamp 100), so these trades could not close at those shops. Shops like ggari-shop and psyoung82 quote near the median, but lower-priced shops are worth checking.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed trades. The 33 of 40 deals could rise to about 36. Average paid share of budget could rise above 82.5%, which is fine, since a deal beats no deal.
ideas.risk: Budgets under the median may have no seller at all, so more search costs time with no result. A cheaper shop could also be low-quality.
ideas.honest: It uses only public prices and the buyer's real budget. It never pays above budget, never fakes a budget and never touches reviews.
ideas.test: Count the share of walked trades, deals per 40 and average paid share of budget before and after, over the next 40 trades. Count how many were rescued at a second shop.

ideas.title: Price-match to the going median on first counter
ideas.what: Our reviews show 2-3 star losses where the seller 'clung' to 105/185/265 or 'stayed at 265' while buyers offered 230 and budgets of 90/160. Going medians are lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260. Lower the opening ask to about the market median plus 5 and set target at the median (never below reserve + 5). Counter once at the median when a buyer's offer is within ~10% of it, instead of conceding 40% of the gap in small steps.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: '2* seller clung to 105 ... budget was 90', '2* seller clung to 185 ... budget 160', '2* seller stayed at 265'. Top shops 11im, lee-sungsoo, JangSeongWoong all have medians at 100/180/260 and win 20%+ share with 4.4+ stars.
ideas.expected: More closed deals per visit (our 135 deals / 253 visits = 53% vs 11im 78%, lee-sungsoo 77%), fewer 2-3 star no-deal reviews, share up; slightly lower average price per deal.
ideas.risk: Lower margin per deal; if reserve is close to the median, little room remains and some buyers still walk.
ideas.honest: Asking prices are real prices we would accept; no false 'was' price, never below reserve + 5, and no claim about other buyers.
ideas.test: A/B by alternating the meta_shop.py opening-ask setting between current and median+5 every 15 min; compare deals/visits and star average over about 300 visits.

ideas.title: Honest 'best price' one-shot close when buyer stalls
ideas.what: When a buyer's stated or implied budget is below our target but above reserve + 5, accept it right away with a signed receipt rather than concede 40% over five rounds. Also state our lowest price truthfully once after the first below-floor offer, so the buyer isn't left to guess ('Our lowest price is X; reply with X to close'). Cut the show-floor threshold from two below-floor offers to one.
ideas.evidence: Reviews '3* Seller would not meet budget' and '2* tried to meet at 230 with service assurance, but seller stayed at 265'. Leeuichann (stars 4.68, best in market) reviews praise 'dropping its asking price from 110... final minimum price 100' and says 'final minimum price 100'. JangSeongWoong closes in few rounds.
ideas.expected: Fewer 5-round no-deals, higher deal rate, stars toward 4.6+ like leeuichann.
ideas.risk: Buyers who would have paid more get the floor sooner, which may lower the average price.
ideas.honest: The stated minimum is genuinely our floor; no fake deadline or scarcity.
ideas.test: Log deal rate and average price among buyers hitting the floor-reveal path before vs after the change over a day.

ideas.title: Fix 429/timeout failures with faster, cheaper responses
ideas.what: Two 1-star reviews are caused by 'Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn: Error 429 rate limit'. Reduce LLM calls per turn: handle price parsing and counteroffers in code, and use Llama 8B only for the short text. Add a deterministic fallback reply (a rule-based counter or accept) when the model call fails or exceeds a time limit, and cache the responses for repeat prompts.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: two '1* Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn: Error code: 429'. Visits 253 vs deals 135.
ideas.expected: Remove 1-star outliers (about 2 in 8 shown reviews), raising stars from 4.5 toward 4.6 and converting more visits to deals.
ideas.risk: Rule-based text is less persuasive; the 429 may originate on the buyer's side and not be fixable by us.
ideas.honest: Only improves reliability; no change in claims or prices.
ideas.test: Count error/1-star reviews and share of visits ending without a receipt per 100 visits, before vs after.

ideas.title: Raise ceiling offer and stop walking from top shops
ideas.what: When budget is at or above the going median but the buyer would otherwise walk, make a final offer at the shop's observed median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) instead of capping at three offers. Pick shops by price tier within budget: for budget 160 chairs, go to shops with median at or below 160 and skip shops that stay at 180+ (11im, lee-sungsoo). Check the budget against the going median first and say up front if no shop sells below the budget.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer: 7 of 40 without a deal, all walked: lee-sungsoo chair budget 160, lee-sungsoo bookshelf 230 (twice), 11im chair budget 160, 11im bookshelf budget 230, bjeon01 bookshelf 230. Going medians are chair 180 and bookshelf 260, so these budgets were below market; we are walking from shops that can never sell at that price.
ideas.expected: Avoid wasted visits; steer low-budget runs to cheaper shops or end early; deal rate up from 33/40 only where a lower-priced shop exists, with average payment near 84% of budget.
ideas.risk: No shop may sell under budget, so some trades still fail; chasing cheap shops may land on shops with weaker reviews or no signed receipts.
ideas.honest: Offers stay at or below the buyer's budget and the 1.1x quartile cap; reviews remain factual.
ideas.test: Compare the walk-away rate and cost per deal over the next 40 trades, split by whether budget was below the median.

ideas.title: Price at the going median, not above it
ideas.what: Our bookshelf deals close at 275 (three 4* reviews cite 275) while the market median is 260 (middle half 260-267) and the top shops sit at 260-263. Lower the bookshelf opening ask and target in meta_shop.py to about the median (260-263), and keep the reserve+5 floor. Check chair and lamp the same way: our reviewed deals at 192 (chair) and 110 (lamp) are above the 180 and 100 medians. Let the quartile logic anchor on the median and stop letting the target drift above the upper quartile.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: 'Bought bookshelf at 275 (budget 325)' x3 and 'fair price 192'. Going prices: bookshelf median 260, chair 180, lamp 100. Our no-deal review: 'seller wanted 105 (budget 90)'. Our buyer skips shops above the upper quartile, so other buyers likely do the same. Our share is 1.5% on 327 visits, and 11im and lee-sungsoo convert about 80% of their visits at median prices.

ideas.risk: Margin shrinks, and if the reserve is close to 260 there is little room. Competitors may drop their own prices in response.
ideas.honest: Only lowers our asks. It stays above reserve+5 and makes no claims about prices or other buyers.
ideas.test: A/B by item over 2 hours: new target vs. current. Compare deals per visit, average price and stars per arm.

ideas.title: Short, verifiable review ask with the exact deal facts
ideas.what: Change the post-deal message to state the facts the buyer can check (item, agreed price, receipt number and that the signature verifies) and make a neutral request: 'If you check the receipt, an honest review of what you found helps other buyers.' Do not ask for a star level, do not offer anything for a review, and do not suggest the content.
ideas.evidence: Reviewers reward matching receipts: 'receipt matched the agreed price', 'Ed25519 receipt verified'. 11im has 2675 reviews for 2675 deals and lee-sungsoo has 2426 for 2426, while we have 189 for 189, so the review rate is already full and quality matters more. nocha12 asks for a 5-star review, which is the kind of conditioning we must not copy.
ideas.expected: Reviews that are more specific and slightly higher in stars (we are at 4.37 against leeuichann's 4.67), which feeds buyer selection by reviews.
ideas.risk: Small effect, and reviewers may ignore it. A longer message could cost tokens on the 8B model, so put it in code, not the prompt.
ideas.honest: States only true facts and asks for an honest review with no incentive or star target.
ideas.test: Compare the mean stars and the share of reviews that mention a verified receipt, before and after, over the next 50 deals.

ideas.title: Plain-language floor disclosure to cut walk-aways and 5-round negotiations
ideas.what: When a buyer is below our floor, say once, clearly, in the first reply: 'Our lowest price today is X, signed receipt, no extras.' Then accept any offer at or above X at once. This replaces the current 'shows the floor after two offers below it' step. Set X to our target, which sits at the market median (see idea 1).
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo's top line: 'the listed price is our lowest, closing in one step with a signed receipt', and its reviews say 'deal after 2 offers'. leeuichann has the best stars, 4.67, with reviews like 'deal after 1 offer'. Our 2* review says 'No deal in 5 round(s)', and our buyer's own walk-aways are mostly from long negotiations at lee-sungsoo.
ideas.expected: Fewer 5-round negotiations and rejected tasks, faster deals, and slightly better stars. Share may rise because buyers' rounds are limited.
ideas.risk: Buyers who like to haggle may leave when they see no room, and we lose the extra margin the 40% concession sometimes captures.
ideas.honest: The disclosed floor is the real floor, so there is no false scarcity or fake deadline.
ideas.test: Compare average rounds per deal, the no-deal rate and stars before and after on a 2-hour split.

ideas.title: Stop re-trying shops where our budget is under their floor, and prefer one-step shops
ideas.what: Add to buyer memory a per-shop, per-item 'walked at budget B' record and a running count of rounds-to-deal. Skip a shop for the same item if we walked from it at a budget at or below the current one within the last N hours. Rank candidates with the fewest median rounds-to-deal and the highest verified-receipt rate (leeuichann, 11im) above shops with the same price but longer negotiations.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer's 8 no-deals include lee-sungsoo bookshelf at budget 230 (walked) four times, and chanarun and leeuichann bookshelf at 230. The bookshelf median is 260 (middle half 260-267), so a 230 budget will not clear a shop whose floor is 260. Our buyer paid 82.8% of budget on average over 32 deals.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted trades (8 of 40 had no deal, which is 20%), so a higher deal rate and lower token cost. Budget is a constraint we cannot raise, so avoiding doomed negotiations is the only lever.
ideas.risk: A shop may lower its prices later, so a permanent skip would miss that. Hence the time window. Fewer tries may also thin the data we use to rank shops.
ideas.honest: Uses only our own factual memory. It does not misstate our budget, and we never offer above it.
ideas.test: Count deals per 40 trades and the share of walked trades before and after, with the same budget mix.

ideas.what: Set the opening ask to the market median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) and make the target equal to it, so a first offer at or near the median is accepted at once. Only keep conceding for buyers who offer below the median. Stop opening above the upper quartile.

The top shops 11im and lee-sungsoo (about 42% of deals combined) sell at the median (lamp 100, chair 180-182, bookshelf 260-262). The reviews of leeuichann mention a 'final minimum price 260' and of nocha12 'lowest I can go 260', so buyers meet a fixed floor at the median.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed negotiations and fewer 2-3* reviews, so stars rise above 4.42. Visit-to-deal conversion rises from 61% (248/404) toward the 78-82% of the leaders, which should lift share. The average price per deal drops a little.

ideas.title: Shorten replies and always include a plain price number
ideas.what: Make the Llama worker output a fixed template: 'Item: X. Price: N. Send your offer as a number.' and after a counteroffer 'Counteroffer: N' or 'Deal: item at N'. Have the code build the number and the sentence, and let the model add at most one short line. Add a retry with a fallback template if the LLM output has no parsable number.

The longer sales-copy replies (yms979, nocha12) belong to shops with fewer deals (5.5%, below 3.1% when long). One of our reviews is a 1* 'Failed to trade' at a harness error.
ideas.expected: Fewer parse failures in buyer agents, more deals per visit, fewer 1-2* reviews. A small stars gain.
ideas.risk: Terse text can feel less friendly and cost some 5* that come from tone. Template bugs would affect every deal.
ideas.honest: It only changes the format. All the numbers stay true and the review request stays honest.
ideas.test: A/B by hour or by item: share of replies with a parsable number, conversion, and share of 'could not agree' reviews.

ideas.title: Open at the market floor on items where rivals hold the floor
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set opening ask equal to target equal to the observed middle-half low (bookshelf 260, chair 180, lamp 100) instead of a higher opening ask with concessions. Keep the code rule of never selling below reserve + 5. Keep the opening line short and factual: 'Asking 260, signed receipt, no added fees.'
ideas.evidence: Top shops lee-sungsoo (21.2% share) and nocha12 open and hold at 260 and say 'one reply accepting it closes the deal'. 11im sells at 260-263. Our reviews: 2* 'Shop refused to budge from 265 despite three reasonable offers' and 2* 'Could not agree on a price', while going median is 260.
ideas.expected: More closed deals per visit (our 271 deals / 441 visits = 61% vs 11im 79%, lee-sungsoo 78%), fewer 2* no-agreement reviews, higher share; per-deal price drops about 2%.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks if reserve is near 260. Buyers with high budgets pay less than they would have.
ideas.honest: The ask is a real price we actually charge, with no false 'was' price. We never go below reserve + 5.
ideas.test: A/B by item across 15-minute meta_shop cycles for 24h: floor-open vs current. Compare deals/visit, stars and revenue per visit.

ideas.title: Reply with a single final price once the buyer is within a few units of it
ideas.what: Add to the shop code: if the buyer's offer is within about 2% of the target, answer with one clear 'Deal at X' or 'Final price X, reply accept' instead of another 40%-of-gap counter. Counters stay at X (no endless rounds). Cap rounds at about 3.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo's reviews show 'deal after 8 offers' and its replies are one-line 'lowest price, one reply accepting it closes the deal'; our 2* review 'Could not agree on a price' and the 429 failures show long negotiations get lost. Buyers' own review: 'nocha12 ... 3 offers until the end'.
ideas.expected: Fewer abandoned negotiations, fewer timeouts under rate limits, deals/visit up toward 75-80%, small star gain.
ideas.risk: Some buyers who would have paid more are closed early; a firm line may cost a few units.
ideas.honest: States a true final price and honors it. The shop never pressures with fake deadlines or scarcity.
ideas.test: Compare mean offers per deal, deals/visit and 1-2* share before and after the change for 24h.

ideas.title: Show receipt number with a real, honored repeat-visit discount
ideas.what: Include the signed receipt number in the deal message and tell the buyer that quoting it on the next visit gives X% off, applied through our existing loyalty code table. Do not ask for or condition anything on reviews in the same sentence.
ideas.evidence: 11im (21.7% share) says 'Receipt No. ...: mention it on your next visit for an extra 3% off' in every deal message. We have loyalty tiers and one-time codes, but our codes are not surfaced as a simple receipt-number mention.
ideas.expected: More repeat visits and a higher share of loyalty-tier orders; share growth over several hours. Cost about 3% on repeat deals.
ideas.risk: Discount may cut into margin below reserve + 5; buyers may not remember to mention it.
ideas.honest: A genuine, honored discount tied to a true receipt; no review conditioning. Dropping the 'please leave a review' line from the same message keeps the discount fully separate from reviews.
ideas.test: Count visits that quote a receipt number, repeat-buyer rate, and margin on those deals over 48h versus the control period.
flags: ties a reward to reviews or stars

ideas.title: Open near the market floor and walk less on tight budgets
ideas.what: In the buyer, start the first offer at the lower middle-half price for the item (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) when the budget is at or above it. When the budget is below every price, skip the 3 offers and move directly to the next shop whose ask is lowest in the ledger, rather than walking from the same shop. Do not retry the same shop twice in a row where it walked.
ideas.evidence: Our last 40 trades: 11 no-deals, mostly 'walked' at lee-sungsoo (chair budget 160, bookshelf budget 230 twice) and dragonash chair 160, while the going median chair is 180 and bookshelf 260; those budgets are below every price. Also the buyer paid 86.1% of budget on average.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted turns and fewer rate-limit failures; no-deal rate down from 27% as budgets below the median are matched to shops that actually concede (e.g. corner-store, yms979, leeuichann closed at 100 on a 105 budget).
ideas.risk: Budgets under the market price may have no seller at all; then walking is correct and the number of no-deals will not fall.
ideas.honest: We offer only within our true budget and never reveal a false budget; skipping shops is not deception.
ideas.test: Track no-deal rate and mean paid/budget over the next 40 trades against the previous 40, split by budget below or above the median.

ideas.title: Fast-close at the going price on first reply
ideas.what: When the buyer's first offer is within ~3% of the target, or the buyer asks for the price, quote and close at the going median in one reply (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) with the signed receipt, instead of running the 40%-of-gap concession loop. Keep the reserve+5 floor in code.

ideas.title: Open at the going median, not above it
ideas.what: Set the opening ask to the market median (lamp 100-105, chair 180, bookshelf 260) instead of the current quartile-based higher opening. Keep target at or near the median; the floor stays reserve+5.

ideas.title: Open at a few percent under the going median and skip the three-offer walk loop for budget-limited trades
ideas.what: Make the buyer's first offer about 3-5% below the shop's posted median, and when the budget is below the shop's floor, stop after one offer and move to the next shop instead of three offers. When a shop has shown a floor (e.g. 'This is our floor'), pay at it right away if within budget.
ideas.evidence: Our 6 failed trades are all with 11im and lee-sungsoo at budgets of 90 (lamp), 230 (bookshelf), 160 (chair), which are below their medians of 100/260/180, so the walks were wasted. ideas.expected: Fewer wasted turns and rate-limit exposure; more trades closed at the going price; the paid fraction of budget may drop slightly.
ideas.risk: Skipping rounds might forgo a shop that would have conceded below its median, such as 11im's lamp at 100 after asking 110 (a 10-credit concession).
ideas.honest: The buyer states real offers within budget and writes factual reviews. It never overbids and never fakes a competing offer.
ideas.test: Log offers per trade, deal rate and paid-to-budget ratio over the next 40 trades and compare with the 34/40 and 81.6% baseline.

ideas.what: Set opening ask for each item at the current market median/lower end of the middle half (bookshelf 260, chair 180, lamp 100) instead of opening higher and conceding. Have the code state one clear, true line: 'this is our lowest price; one reply closes it with a signed receipt', and accept any offer at or above target immediately.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo (22.2% share, 4.46 stars) opens at 180 for chairs and says 'already the lowest price ... one reply at that price gets you the signed receipt'. ideas.expected: Higher deal rate per visit (we convert 342/538 = 64% vs lee-sungsoo 78%) and more share; slightly lower average price per deal, offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Margin falls if the reserve is close to the median; buyers with high budgets pay less than they would have.

ideas.title: Budget-aware walk-away close for low-budget buyers
ideas.what: When a buyer's offers are below the floor and they have refused twice, state the true floor once plainly and add a final 'last offer' message with the exact lowest acceptable price (reserve+5), instead of 5 rounds of small concessions. If the buyer reveals a budget at or above the floor, accept it right away.
ideas.evidence: Our review: 'No deal after 5 round(s): seller clung to 185 with no flexible service while my budget was 160'. Ours-vs-others: leeuichann (4.65 stars) says 'final minimum price 260' and closes quickly; reviews reward quick, clear negotiations ('closed the deal at my final offer').
ideas.expected: Fewer 2* reviews from failed negotiations, higher average stars (we are 4.46 vs leeuichann 4.65), and recovery of some deals that end at the floor.
ideas.risk: Low-budget buyers may walk anyway; revealing the floor early removes room to extract above-floor prices from others.
ideas.honest: The floor we state is the actual one; we never sell below reserve + 5 and make no false claims about it.
ideas.test: Log outcome by negotiation length; compare rate of 1-2* reviews and deals closed at floor before vs after for a day.

ideas.title: Prefer shops with proven flat-fair pricing and open near the median
ideas.what: Rank shops using the observed median/opening vs the market median, favouring shops whose opening is at the median (lee-sungsoo, leeuichann, dragonash, nocha12 at 260). Make the first offer about 90-93% of the median (capped by budget) rather than a lower anchor, then raise to close, so one or two offers settle.
ideas.evidence: 7 of our last 40 trades ended without a deal, 5 of them against lee-sungsoo, which holds firm at 180/260 (chair budget 160 walked three times, bookshelf budget 230 walked). Those budgets are below the going price (median 180, 260), so haggling against a firm shop wastes trades. Average spend 84.6% of budget on deals.
ideas.expected: Fewer walked trades and wasted effort; price paid stays near median.
ideas.risk: Slightly higher paid price than aggressive lowballing against flexible shops like corner-store or ggari-shop.
ideas.honest: Uses only public ledger and our own budget; we never offer above budget and write factual reviews.
ideas.test: Track no-deal rate and paid/budget over the next 40 trades versus the 33/40 baseline.

ideas.title: Skip a shop for an item when budget is below its firm floor
ideas.what: Before visiting, compare the buyer's budget with the shop's published/observed price for that item (e.g. lee-sungsoo chair 180, lamp 100). If the budget is below the shop's observed median and the shop has shown it never moves, go straight to a flexible shop (corner-store, ggari-shop, willow-goods) or one that counter-offers below market, instead of making the three-offer walk.
ideas.evidence: lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 walked three times, lee-sungsoo bookshelf budget 230 walked, 11im lamp budget 90 walked; lee-sungsoo's own line: '180 is already the lowest price ... we can give you'. Willow-goods countered 198 and 216 on chairs, showing some shops move.
ideas.expected: Fewer no-deal trades (7 of 40 now), faster closings, no extra price paid.
ideas.risk: Budgets under the market median may have no willing seller anywhere; we may skip a shop that could have conceded.
ideas.honest: Choice is based on public evidence and our memory, no pressure or deception toward any shop.
ideas.test: Count no-deal trades where budget < shop's known floor before and after; target at most 3 of 40.

ideas.title: Chair target down to market floor 180
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py set the chair target (accept-at-or-above) and floor to the going median 180 (never below reserve+5), and stop the 185 counteroffer plateau. Keep opening ask modestly above, but let the code close at 180 when a buyer reaches it.
ideas.evidence: Our reviews: 2* 'Would not come below 185 for the chair; corner-store offered it for 180. No deal.' and 2* 'repeatedly counteroffering 185 despite my increments from 130 to my budget limit of 160'. Going chair median 180 (middle half 180-183); top shops 11im/lee-sungsoo/dragonash all close chairs at 180.
ideas.expected: More chair deals converted, fewer 2* reviews, stars up from 4.43 toward 4.5, share up a little; small per-deal margin loss on chairs offset by volume.
ideas.risk: Reserve plus 5 may exceed 180 for some orders, so those still fail; margin shrinks if buyers would have paid 185 anyway.
ideas.honest: Only lowers a real price; never goes below reserve+5; no false claims.
ideas.test: A/B by 15-minute cycle: chair target 185 vs 180; compare chair conversion rate (deals/visits), average star rating on chair reviews, and margin per chair over ~200 visits.

ideas.title: Plain fixed-price quick close for budget-limited buyers
ideas.what: When a buyer's offer is within the accept band or their stated budget is below our target but at or above reserve+5, accept immediately and say the true price rather than countering again. Also state truthfully in the first reply 'our lowest price is X, signed receipt' for items already priced at the median (lamp 100, bookshelf 260).
ideas.evidence: 11im (21.3% share) replies 'Deal: lamp at 100' directly; lee-sungsoo states '180 is the fixed listed price... confirming closes the sale right away'; leeuichann has the best stars 4.64 with 'final minimum price 260'. Our visits-to-deals ratio is 376/579 (65%) vs 11im 4032/5128 (79%).
ideas.expected: Higher visit-to-deal conversion (target 75%+), fewer walked negotiations, modest share gain.
ideas.risk: Leaves a few credits on the table with buyers who would have paid more; the 'lowest price' statement must really be the lowest we would accept.
ideas.honest: Only states the actual floor price; no fake scarcity or 'was' price.
ideas.test: Compare conversion rate and average sale price before and after on the same item over 24h; check reviews for 'unwilling to negotiate' complaints.

ideas.title: Prefer cheaper shops at the median instead of walking
ideas.what: When the budget is below the ask at the first-choice shop, rank alternatives by public ledger median for that item and try the next shop in the list (e.g. median-price shops 11im, lee-sungsoo, dragonash, leeuichann) before walking, and do not retry a shop that already walked us three times for the same item/budget.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer's 7 no-deals include lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 walked three times in a row, and 25620027 bookshelf walked; chair median is 180 so a 160 budget can never close at lee-sungsoo. Going prices are tightly clustered (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260).
ideas.expected: Fewer repeated failed trades and a higher deal rate than 33/40; the average paid share of budget may go up slightly. Budget below the market median simply means no deal and should be recorded as such.
ideas.risk: If the budget is below every price, no shop will close; we waste turns. Avoiding a shop could miss a price drop.
ideas.honest: Uses only public ledger data and our own memory; no pressure or misreporting; budget never exceeded.
ideas.test: Track repeated (shop, item, budget) walk-aways per 40 trades; target zero repeats and no drop in deal rate.

ideas.title: Retry-with-backoff on 429 and exclude infrastructure errors
ideas.what: Wrap buyer_turn with exponential backoff and jitter on 429s, cap concurrent trades, and mark infrastructure failures separately so they do not turn into reviews or shop penalties.
ideas.evidence: Our shop reviews include 1* 'Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn: Error code: 429 ... Rate limit reached'; our buyer's no-deal list includes '25620027 bookshelf budget 295 (error)'.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed trades and one fewer source of 1* reviews on our shop, which protects stars (4.43) and avoids lost deals.
ideas.risk: Backoff slows throughput; retries could duplicate an order if not idempotent.
ideas.honest: Only reduces our own load on the service and makes trades succeed; no deception.
ideas.test: Count 429/error outcomes per 100 trades before and after; confirm no duplicate receipts for one order id.

ideas.title: Budget-aware final ask instead of walking away
ideas.what: When the buyer's last offer is below our floor-adjacent price but within a small gap (e.g. under 5%) of the lowest price we may legally accept (reserve + 5), have the shop code make one final counter at exactly reserve + 5 rather than showing the floor and letting the buyer walk. Keep the rule: never below reserve + 5, never above the buyer's stated budget.
ideas.evidence: Reviews of our shop: 3* 'No deal: lowest ask 270 stayed above my budget 230', 2* 'The seller's counteroffer of 185 exceeds my 160 budget', 2* 'Could not agree on a price'. We have 392 deals from 621 visits (63%) versus 11im 4268/5451 (78%) and lee-sungsoo 4238/5502 (77%), so lost visits are our main gap.
ideas.expected: Raise deal conversion from about 63% toward 70%+, adding deals and share. Average price drops slightly on those converted visits, and no-deal 2-3* reviews should fall.
ideas.risk: Some buyers who would have paid more now settle at the lowest allowed price, cutting margin; a final-ask rule could also leak the floor to later buyers if shared.
ideas.honest: Sells only at or above reserve + 5 and within the buyer's budget; the final ask is a true statement of the lowest price we accept, with no invented scarcity or deadlines.
ideas.test: A/B by visit parity for 2 hours: compare deal rate, mean price/reserve margin, and star average of no-deal reviews between the two arms.

ideas.title: Tighter opening asks near the market median
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py, lower the opening ask for each item to roughly the upper end of the middle half (lamp about 105, chair about 185, bookshelf about 266) instead of the higher openings that lead to 270/185 counters against 230/160 budgets. Keep target and reserve logic unchanged.
ideas.evidence: Going prices: lamp 100-105, chair 180-185, bookshelf 260-266. The top shops open near those numbers (lee-sungsoo 'fixed listed price 180', 25620027 'lamp asking 100'). Our losses cite asks of 270 and 185 above budgets.
ideas.expected: Fewer budget-based walkouts in the buyer's first look, higher visit-to-deal ratio and better review text about fair opening prices. Slightly lower average price per deal.
ideas.risk: Margin per deal falls if buyers would have accepted higher openings; the median could move and leave us stale between 15-minute refreshes.
ideas.honest: Asks are real prices we are willing to sell at, drawn from observed market quartiles, with no fake 'was' price.
ideas.test: Compare visit-to-deal rate and average deal price over 3 hours before/after the change, with the market median recorded as a control.

ideas.title: Retry a walked shop with one extra offer up to the budget cap
ideas.what: When our buyer would walk after three offers because its budget is below the shop's price, check whether the budget is already at or above the shop's publicly shown floor or the item's going median; if it is, make one more offer at the budget (never above it, never above 1.1 x upper quartile) before leaving. Otherwise switch shops at once instead of repeating attempts at a shop that will not meet budget.
ideas.evidence: Buyer: 7 of the last 40 trades had no deal, including lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 walked three times in a row, 11im lamp budget 90 walked, and 25620027 bookshelf budget 230 walked. Going chair median is 180 and lamp 100, so those budgets were below market; repeating the same shop was wasted effort.
ideas.expected: Fewer failed trades from the same shop-budget combination, so higher deal rate (from 33/40 to maybe 36/40) with unchanged payment ratio of about 84% of budget.
ideas.risk: The extra offer at budget could raise the average amount paid; skipping a shop after a failure may miss a later price drop.
ideas.honest: Offers stay at or below our own budget and within the cap; the buyer's reviews remain factual about what happened.
ideas.test: Track repeated walk-aways per shop-item-budget in the buyer log and compare deal rate and percentage of budget paid over the next 40 trades.

ideas.title: Prefer shops with high deal rate and matching receipts, ranked by stars per visit
ideas.what: Add visits-to-deals conversion and stars from the public ledger into the buyer's shop choice score, together with price. For under-market budgets, favor shops whose medians sit at or below the going median (dragonash 100/260/180, 25620027 final price 100) and deprioritize ones that repeatedly said no to us (lee-sungsoo for chairs at budget 160).
ideas.evidence: Ledger shows conversion differences: leeuichann 693/1209 (57%) despite 4.64 stars versus 11im 78% and dragonash 1674/2106 (79%). Our buyer's three walks at lee-sungsoo, which holds 'fixed listed price 180', happened with budget 160.
ideas.expected: Higher deal completion, with paid share of budget staying near 84% or improving; fewer wasted rounds with shops that hold firm above our budget.
ideas.risk: Overweighting conversion could steer all buying to a few shops and ignore a cheaper newcomer; ledger stats are a lagging signal.
ideas.honest: Uses only public ledger data and our own memory, and review text we write stays factual about each outcome.
ideas.test: Log the choice score alongside outcome for 50 trades and compare deal rate and paid/budget versus the current picker.

ideas.title: Visible-floor first reply for low-budget buyers
ideas.what: When a buyer's first offer is below the floor, state the true floor (reserve+5) and the signed-receipt promise in the first reply, instead of conceding in small steps over several rounds. Cap negotiation at 2-3 rounds with a clear final price, as leeuichann ('final minimum price 260') and yms979 ('This is our floor, we never sell below it') do.
ideas.evidence: Our 2* reviews: 'No deal after 5 round(s): seller clung to 185 ... my budget was 160' and 'tried to meet at 90 ... seller stayed at 105'. Top shops quote a clear floor quickly (yms979, dragonash 'Counteroffer: 100').
ideas.expected: Fewer drawn-out no-deals and fewer 2* reviews; modest stars gain (4.42 toward 4.5+), small share gain from faster closes.
ideas.risk: Revealing the floor early may cost a few dollars of margin on buyers who would have paid more.
ideas.honest: Only states real prices and the real floor; no false scarcity or deadlines; never sells below reserve+5.
ideas.test: A/B by item or by hour: compare average rounds to close, no-deal rate, share of 2* or lower reviews, and margin per deal over about 200 visits each.

ideas.title: Rate-limit-safe lighter replies (fewer LLM calls)
ideas.what: Handle routine turns (counteroffer, floor statement, deal confirmation, thank-you) with deterministic templates in code and call Llama only for free-form questions. Add a cheap retry/backoff on our own side and a short response timeout.
ideas.evidence: Our 1* review: 'Failed to trade: RuntimeError: Harness failed after 5 attempts for buyer_turn ... 429'. Visits 694 vs deals 438 means about 37% of visits end without a deal. Top shops 11im and lee-sungsoo reply with near-identical templated lines ('Deal: lamp at 100. Receipt No. ...').
ideas.expected: Recover some of the 256 non-deal visits; remove error-type failed trades; slightly higher conversion (deals/visits) and stars.
ideas.risk: Templated text can feel robotic and lose the occasional upsell; if the failure was on the buyer's harness side, gain is smaller.
ideas.honest: Same prices and rules, only faster and more reliable delivery; nothing claimed that is untrue.
ideas.test: Track deals/visits and error-flagged results before and after for 24 hours; compare against the 694/438 baseline.

ideas.title: Match the market-median price on lamps/chairs/bookshelves exactly (no opening premium)
ideas.what: In meta_shop.py, set opening ask equal to the observed median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) with target equal to the lower end of the middle half, and have a stated honest 'final' price. Keep the launch-sale logic. Do not open higher than the upper quartile.
ideas.evidence: Going prices: lamp 100 (100-105), chair 180 (180-185), bookshelf 260 (260-270). The shops with the biggest shares (11im, lee-sungsoo) deal at exactly those medians; corner-store (chair 187, bookshelf 275) and ggari-shop (bookshelf asking 315) have much smaller shares. Our reviews show bookshelf sold at 275 and lamp 110, above median.
ideas.expected: Higher deal count and share per visit; a lower average price (roughly 3-5%) offset by volume; the buyer-side filter 'above upper quartile' stops excluding us.
ideas.risk: Margin shrinks; a race to the floor if rivals cut further.
ideas.honest: Real prices only, based on public medians; no invented 'was' price.
ideas.test: Run for 3 hours with the new table; compare deals per visit and share against the previous 3 hours, and check that margin stays above reserve+5.

ideas.title: Prefer top-share shops with fast closes and skip repeat-walk shops
ideas.what: Add to buyer memory a per-shop walk count: after two walks at the same shop for an item with a budget below its floor, stop visiting that shop for that budget class and route to the shop whose public median fits the budget (e.g. 11im, dragonash, leeuichann). Also pre-check the budget against the market median before visiting and skip when the budget is below median.
ideas.evidence: Buyer no-deals: lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 (walked) three times, 11im lamp budget 90 (walked), 25620027 bookshelf budget 230 (walked) and 295 (error); going chair median is 180, lamp 100, bookshelf 260, so these budgets were below every price.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted trades (7 of 40 failed now, about 17%); deal rate rises toward 90%+ where budgets allow; no change in price paid.
ideas.risk: Budgets below every price will fail regardless; skipping may reduce data on whether prices drop.
ideas.honest: Purely a choice of whom to visit; no deception and never exceeds budget or 1.1x upper quartile.
ideas.test: Count repeat walks per shop over the next 40 trades and compare the deal rate against the 33/40 baseline.

ideas.title: Mention-us returning-buyer discount like 11im
ideas.what: Add a true, signed follow-up incentive in the deal message: 'mention receipt No. X on your next visit for an extra 3% off', honored by code through the existing one-time loyalty code (never below reserve + 5). Use a flat 3% on the second visit, separate from the 1-6 tier table, and apply it only when the resulting price stays above the floor.
ideas.evidence: 11im (4801 deals, 20.8% share) ends every deal with 'Receipt No. ...: mention it on your next visit for an extra 3% off', while our share is 1.9% on 703 visits and our reviews show buyers returning at 105 on repeat rounds.
ideas.expected: Higher repeat visits and conversion per visit (445 deals / 703 visits is 63%, vs 11im 78%); modest share gain, small price give-up of about 3% on returns only.
ideas.risk: Margin loss on repeat buyers who would have paid full price anyway; overlap with tier discounts could stack below floor if the code doesn't cap it.
ideas.honest: The discount is real, honored by code, and stated exactly; no review is requested in exchange or conditioned on it, and the floor stays at reserve + 5.
ideas.test: A/B by receipt parity for 2 days: half get the 3% line. Compare return-visit rate, deals per visit and average margin.

ideas.title: Match the going lamp/chair/bookshelf price exactly on first counter
ideas.what: Set opening ask and counter for each item to the middle-half lower bound (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) after the first offer, rather than conceding 40% of the gap in steps. Keep a slightly higher opening ask only on bookshelf where the quartile range is 260-270, and quote one fixed 'listed price' that we really charge.
ideas.evidence: Going prices: lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260. Top shops 11im, lee-sungsoo, dragonash, ggari-shop and nocha12 all counter at exactly 100/180/260, and corner-store, which sits above (chair 187, lamp 104), has only 6.1% share. Our reviews show lamp deals at 110 and bookshelf at 275, above the median.
ideas.expected: Fewer walk-aways and fewer multi-round negotiations (reviews note 2-3 rounds); likely a bump in share with about 5% lower average price on bookshelf and lamp.
ideas.risk: Gives up margin on buyers who would have paid 105-110; collapses to price parity with no differentiation.
ideas.honest: Prices are real, no fake 'was' price or scarcity claims; reserve + 5 floor is untouched.
ideas.test: Change meta_shop.py targets for 24 hours; compare deals per visit, average price paid and share against the previous 24 hours.

ideas.title: Short, fixed-price replies to cut buyer-side failures and latency
ideas.what: Have code, not the Llama 8B, produce the counteroffer and deal text from templates ('X is too low. Counteroffer: N.' / 'Deal: lamp at N. Receipt No. ...'), and call the model only for an optional one-line description. Return quickly and avoid heavy model calls per turn.
ideas.evidence: Winners dragonash, ggari-shop, 11im and JangSeongWoong use terse templated replies ('89 is too low. Counteroffer: 100.'; 'Deal: lamp at 100.'). Our reviews include two 1* 'Failed to trade' entries after harness failures, and 4* reviews that mention speed ('quick deal (1s)').
ideas.expected: Fewer failed trades and 1* reviews, a slightly higher star average (4.42 toward 4.48) and a higher conversion rate.
ideas.risk: Plainer text may lose some of the warm tone that buyers' review prompts appreciate; template bugs could mis-state a price.
ideas.honest: Every number in the reply is computed by the same pricing code, so the message always matches the receipt.
ideas.test: Compare the rate of error/1* reviews and the mean response time for 500 visits before and after the change.

ideas.title: Avoid shops with repeated walk-aways and cap budgets by item median
ideas.what: Add a short per-shop memory: after one walk against a shop for an item at a budget below its floor, skip that shop for that item and budget band for a few hours, and go to a shop whose observed median is at or below budget (e.g. 11im/lee-sungsoo for chair only when budget is at least 180). When budget is under the going median, go straight to the cheapest shop with a lower-than-median report, such as 25620027 for lamp at 100.
ideas.evidence: Our buyer's 7 non-deals: lee-sungsoo chair budget 160 walked three times, 11im lamp budget 90 walked, 25620027 bookshelf walked/error. Going prices (chair 180, lamp 100) are above those budgets, and the buyer paid 84.1% of budget on average.
ideas.expected: Fewer wasted trades (7 of 40 failed), more deals per trade; no change in the price paid.
ideas.risk: Some budgets are simply below market, so no shop will sell; a skip list can wrongly exclude a shop whose prices dropped later.
ideas.honest: Uses only our own observed outcomes and public prices; no deception or pressure on shops, and the buyer never offers above budget.
ideas.test: Run the buyer for the next 40 trades with the skip rule and compare the no-deal rate with the 7/40 baseline.

ideas.title: Open at the market median and skip shops priced above it
ideas.what: Make the buyer's first offer the going median (lamp 100, chair 180, bookshelf 260) and prefer shops whose median matches (11im, lee-sungsoo, dragonash, ggari-shop, our own shop), skipping corner-store/yms979 type shops 4-7% above. ideas.risk: A median open may be refused by shops with higher floors, costing a round trip.

ideas.title: Rotate toward our own shop never; instead check posted price before offering
